But exp89r's later UP shows that its unrounded score is above exp89p's, and R26-A4 (d) ('chains by completion order') and card step 9's swap rule ('equal with attributable UP -> becomes V_pub') both pick exp89r. The freeze (9) precedent (exp89p vs exp85a at 0.958, code 0 -> 'stays exp85a (fewer levers)') decides at (3), not on exp85a's older UP 21. That supports the finding's reading that an UP earned at a lower display does not rank files within the new display. The choice matters: it picks the V_pub final and switches the pair between P3 {exp87a, #37} and P1 {exp89p, exp75}, which also puts SEC into a final (allowed only as V_pub under Q3). The flaw is that the proposed pairwise sentence ('X above Y iff X completed after Y with UP; the rest by (2)-(4)') is not transitive and can cycle. Example: exp89r reads 0.959 with an UP, so it sits above exp87a. exp89l then reads 0.959 with k=0, so it sits above exp89r by (3) (4 levers < 5), and exp87a sits above exp89l by (3) (3 < 4). That leaves no top file. On value: this only settles a process ambiguity. It does not raise the expected private score, which of exp87a (K+CI) and exp89p (K+SEC) is better on private is close to a coin flip (CI has two + LB reads, SEC has a weak negative lab prior), and the gain is simply that the final pick does not depend on how someone reads the card at 12:03Z.

Use a running-champion form instead of the pairwise form: 'TIE ORDER (1) = R26-A4 (d), sequential. Go through the top-display COMPLETE files in completion order. The first one is the champion. A later file C replaces the champion iff C's own completion gave an attributable UP (k >= 1 with the count check, or under the R26-A4 (b) exemption), because that UP shows C beats every earlier file. Otherwise (k = 0 / MASKED / BLIND) C and the champion are unresolved and the champion is chosen by (2) non-CI, (3) fewer levers, (4) earlier submit. This reading replaces the literal "last attributable UP at that display" of CONTEXT l.3181 and matches freeze (9) and card step 9.'
